PART A
```{r}
score <- 78

if (score >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
} else {
  print("Failed")
}

score <- 86

if (score >= 90) {
  print("Excellent")
} else if (score >= 80) {
  print("Good")
} else if (score >= 75) {
  print("Fair")
} else {
  print("Needs Improvement")
}

scores <- c(92, 68, 75, 81, 59)
ifelse(scores >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")

grade <- 91
attendance <- 95

if (grade >= 90 & attendance >= 90) {
  print("Honors candidate")
}
```

```{r}
#Question 4
x <- 10

if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}
# The result is "A", since x is 10 then 10 > 5 is TRUE.
# R stops at the first TRUE so the other branches are skipped, so it prints "A".

#Question 5
# if checks one value, while ifelse checks a whole vector.
# Use if for one decision or to run many lines and Use ifelse for a column of data.
```

F.
```{r}
grades$FinalGrade <- 0.30 * grades$Quiz + 0.30 * grades$Midterm + 0.40 * grades$Final

grades$Result <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                 ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed"))

grades$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement")))))

grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")

grades$Honors <- ifelse(!is.na(grades$FinalGrade) & grades$FinalGrade >= 90 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Yes", "No")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grades))) {
  if (is.na(grades$FinalGrade[i])) {
    print(paste(grades$Name[i], "Incomplete"))
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 75) {
    print(paste(grades$Name[i], "Passed"))
  } else {
    print(paste(grades$Name[i], "Failed"))
  }
}


#if (grades$FinalGrade >= 75) print("Passed")
# if needs one TRUE or FALSE and FinalGrade >= 75 gives 15 values.
# Newer R gives an error, while Older R gives a warning
# and uses only the first value. The loop checks one row at a time
# so each condition is a single value.

table(grades$Result)
table(grades$AttendanceFlag)
table(grades$Honors)
# 10 student passed, while 4 students failed.
# Theres 1 incomplete students and 4 at risk.
# And there's 4 Honors candidates.

ncol(grades)
```

PART D
```{r}
#Question 7
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)

at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No at-risk students")
}

honors <- grades[grades$Honors == "Yes", c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No honors candidates")
}

check_full <- read.csv("students_grades_processed.csv")
check_risk <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv")
check_honors <- read.csv("honors_list.csv")

dim(check_full)
dim(grades)
nrow(check_risk) == nrow(at_risk)
nrow(check_honors) == nrow(honors)
head(check_full)

#Question 8
write.csv(grades, "temp_with_rownames.csv")
head(read.csv("temp_with_rownames.csv"))
file.remove("temp_with_rownames.csv")
# The missing midterm shows as NA and the FinalGrade is also NA.
# Result says Incomplete because without row.names it's FALSE.
# R adds an extra first column, holds the numbers 1 to 15 and has an empty or X header
```

Question 9
```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Pending",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Full",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Partial", "None")))

scholars <- grades[grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"), ]

if (nrow(scholars) > 0) {
  write.csv(scholars, "scholarship_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No scholarship candidates")
}

table(grades$Scholarship)
```

QUestion 10
```{r}
# 1. I checked is.na() first because NA >= 75 gives NA, and if cannot work with NA, so it would #cause an error.

# 2. If Failed came before Incomplete, the student with the missing grade would get NA instead of #Incomplete, because a missing grade is neither TRUE nor FALSE.

# 3. ifelse() is better for a whole column of data, while if ... else is better for a single value #or when running several lines of code, like writing a file.

# 4. Reading the CSV back confirms the file saved correctly, with the right rows and columns, the #NA values kept, and no extra column.
```
